html:
The Tsimshian (Ts'msyen) are a people of the northern coast of British Columbia and southern Alaska, around the lower Skeena River and the coast and islands near Prince Rupert. Their lands (laxyuup) are held by house groups within four clans, and names, crests and land pass through the mother's line, shown and confirmed at feasts.

They lived on salmon, eulachon fish oil, sea mammals and cedar, and traded the prized eulachon grease along "grease trails" into the interior. The fourteen tribes include Kitsumkalum and Gitxaała.

In 1834 the Hudson's Bay Company moved Fort Simpson, now Lax Kw'alaams, onto their coast, and it became a trading centre for the whole region. The missionary William Duncan founded a model Christian village at Metlakatla in 1862 and in 1887 led many of its people to New Metlakatla in Alaska. Their neighbours include the Nisga'a and Gitxsan, who speak related languages, and the Haida across the water.
